name: io.github.assafbar2/agentswitchboard
description: In-browser WebMCP tools for Agent Switchboard, registered on document.modelContext when the page loads. Same seven read tools as the remote MCP server at /api/mcp: search_agents, get_agent, list_categories, compare_agents, alternatives_to, connect_bundle and recommend. They call the public REST API (/api/agents, /api/agents/{slug}, /api/categories, /api/compare, /api/agents/{slug}/alternatives, /api/bundle, /api/recommend), so answers and their order are the same as the remote server's; result objects use the REST field names (see /openapi.json).

tools.name: search_agents
tools.description: Search the curated Agent Switchboard directory of AI agents, MCP servers, and agentic tools. Filter by task, category slug, access methods, official (first-party listings from major vendors), verified, and/or auth type; sort by relevance, newest, most skills, or name. Verified: we checked it works — its URLs load and its declared access (API, MCP, CLI or extension) responds. Re-checked monthly; the label drops if it stops working. Official: a first-party listing, published by the company behind the product under its own domain or GitHub org (e.g. Notion's own Notion MCP, not a community build), where that company is a major vendor (publicly traded, a frontier AI lab, or valued around $1B+). It records who publishes the product, not a paid placement, and is separate from Verified.

tools.name: compare_agents
tools.description: Put 2 or 3 listings side by side, as the site's /compare page does. For each listing: the facts that set it apart from the others ("Only one with a CLI", "No auth required", "Most skills (12)"). Then one row per field, with each listing's value by slug: what it is, provider, official vendor, verified, access, auth, MCP server, CLI install, API base URL, skills, streaming, push, categories, tags, listed since. A row where every listing agrees has same: true. Facts from the listings' own data, never a verdict. A curated comparison of the same listings adds its intro line. Unknown or repeated slugs, and any past 3, are left out with a note.

tools.name: alternatives_to
tools.description: Listings that could stand in for one listing, strongest first, as on its /agents/<slug>/alternatives page. Each alternative is in the listing's main category, offers at least one of its access methods, and overlaps on what it does (shared skills and tags, rarer ones counting for more). Each comes with why: the access methods both offer and what they have in common. Up to 8. Fewer, or none, rather than a weak match. Also returns a link comparing the listing with its top two alternatives.

tools.name: connect_bundle
tools.description: One MCP client config to paste ({"mcpServers": …}, as Cursor and other MCP clients read it) for up to 10 listings, and how each one connects. A listing is in the config when its own docs give a hosted server address or a local command. An MCP server whose docs give neither comes with its setup guide, and setupPrompt asks a coding agent to set all of those up. A listing without an MCP server comes with its CLI install command, API address or docs. Also returns a claude mcp add command for each server in the config, for Claude Code, and the /stack link for the listings. Nothing is guessed: every address and command is copied from the vendor's docs, as on the listing's page.

tools.name: recommend
tools.description: One recommendation for what your user needs, and the next step to start using it, as the site's Operator (/operator) picks it. Pass the need in a sentence you write yourself, e.g. "query Postgres and send email": each need it names gets one pick, why it fits, the next step (the MCP client config to paste when the vendor's docs give one, else its setup guide or docs) and two alternatives; two or more picks also come with a /stack link. Name a product to prefer the listings that mention it; say MCP, CLI, API, browser extension or official to narrow the pick. Picked by fixed matching rules, not a model, so the same need always gets the same answer. A need that matches no task is refused with the closest tasks. Never include names, email addresses or phone numbers.
